Compare state taxonomies on held-out trajectory blocks

Source: R/state-comparison.R
compare_ssf_states.Rd

Every candidate uses the same observations, controls and validation blocks. All starts are fitted on training data only. The highest training likelihood among numerically eligible starts is retained before applying the taxonomy. The full-data fit supplies the labels. Held-out scores integrate over states and start each independent segment at the fitted stationary distribution.

Usage

compare_ssf_states(
  data,
  taxonomies,
  blocks = ssf_blocks(data),
  step_families = NULL,
  n_starts = 5L,
  initializers = NULL,
  short_iter = 60L,
  long_iter = 400L,
  seed = 1L,
  workers = 1L,
  engine = c("native", "R"),
  normalization = c("importance", "exact"),
  assessment_args = list(),
  score_tolerance = 0.01,
  objective_tolerance = 1e-07,
  score_failed_hessian = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Prepared ssf_data (importance normalisation) or ssf_steps (exact normalisation). Segment IDs must be independent uninterrupted runs.

taxonomies

Nonempty list of ssf_taxonomy() objects with distinct names. The number of labels determines each candidate's state count.

blocks

Named integer vector assigning each segment to a block. Values must be consecutive integers starting at one. Default is three chronological blocks made by ssf_blocks(). No segment is split.

step_families

Character vector of explicit positive length families, or NULL for the canonical gamma formula. Candidates cross families and taxonomies. Keep the same observation density measure throughout.

n_starts

Number of independently polished starts per training fit when initializers is NULL.

initializers

Optional function with arguments data, taxonomy, step_family, seed and block. It receives training rows only and returns a nonempty named list of initial_values for fit_ssf(). Block zero denotes the full-data fit. It replaces n_starts.

short_iter, long_iter, engine, normalization

Passed to fit_ssf(). Only homogeneous transitions and lengths without lag terms are supported.

seed

Nonnegative integer. Per-job seeds are recorded. The caller's random state is restored, including with parallel workers.

workers

Number of processes on Unix. Other platforms run serially.

assessment_args

Named arguments for assess_taxonomy(), excluding fit, taxonomy, convention and score_tolerance.

score_tolerance, objective_tolerance

Numerical eligibility thresholds.

score_failed_hessian

Also report a separate point-prediction score that allows a failed Hessian check. Convergence, gradient, kernel and objective agreement checks still apply. It does not replace strict scores.

Value

An ssf_state_comparison with candidates, block_scores, segment_scores, starts, full-data fits and assessments, and the supplied specifications. start_profiles and start_coefficients retain movement summaries and coefficients of every successful start, including rejected ones. length_rank aligns them descriptively, not biologically. A pooled score is NA unless every block was scored. taxonomy_passed refers to the full-data fit, not prediction. Scores are conditional log choice probabilities for importance models, or log densities for exact models. Higher is better on identical rows. This comparison does not identify a true biological number of states.
